description: The machine-checkable half of docs/__meta__/arch-prd.md#2-frontmatter and docs/__meta__/arch-prd.md#3-sections. No section has a word cap and the file has no token budget.

name.description: prd-<NNN>-<feature>: the document number docs/__meta__/arch.md allocates, one sequence shared by every document in docs/arch/, then the feature in a few kebab-case words. See docs/__meta__/arch-prd.md#1-naming.

status.description: approved once no open question is left; frozen once shipped or dropped.

outline.description: Who needs the feature, what they cannot do today, and why it matters now, in one or two paragraphs.
examples:
A repository that adopts Lorecraft writes its meta specs before its documents, and until the first document
lands, a check reports nothing at all. A writer cannot tell a corpus that passes from one that is not checked.

outline.description: The outcomes the feature commits to, as a bulleted list.
examples:
- A writer sees, on every run, which documents no meta spec governs.
- A broken meta spec stops the run before any document is read.

outline.description: What a reader might expect the feature to do and it does not, each with the reason it is out of scope.
examples: - Repairing a broken meta spec: the check reports it, and the writer fixes it.

outline.description: Prioritised user stories, each under an H3 that gives its identifier, title and priority, each with an independent test and one or more scenarios, each a gherkin block of its own holding one Scenario: and no Feature:.
examples:
### US-1: See what is unchecked (P1)

As a writer adopting Lorecraft, I want every ungoverned document reported, so that I know which ones no check
reads.

**Independent test:** Check a workspace with documents and no meta spec.

```gherkin
Scenario: No corpus has a meta spec
  Given a workspace with no meta spec
  When the writer checks it
  Then every document is reported as unvalidated
```

outline.description: Numbered FR- and NFR- items, one behaviour each, each in one EARS pattern; an unknown is marked [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …] inline.
examples:
- **FR-001:** THE SYSTEM SHALL report every finding with the path of the document it was found in.
- **FR-002:** WHEN a user checks a workspace that holds no meta spec, THE SYSTEM SHALL report every document
  as unvalidated.
- **NFR-001:** THE SYSTEM SHALL check a workspace of 1,000 documents in under two seconds.

outline.description: Boundary conditions and failure paths the user stories do not cover, as questions.
examples: - What happens when a workspace holds a meta spec but no document?

outline.description: The concepts the requirements name, what each is to the user and how it relates to the others, without its representation.
examples:
- **Document:** A file under a corpus, governed by the meta specs its path selects.
- **Meta spec:** The rules for a group of documents, selected by its name.

outline.description: Numbered SC- items, each a measurable outcome stated without naming the technology.
examples:
- **SC-001:** A writer adopting Lorecraft finds every unchecked document from one run's output, with no other
  command.

outline.description: What the requirements take for granted, as a bulleted list.
examples: - Every document sits directly in its corpus directory, not in a subdirectory of it.

outline.description: Every [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker in the document, gathered under the identifier of the requirement that carries it.
examples: - **FR-006:** In every output format, or in the text output only?

outline.description: The issue the PRD comes from, as Source, and the design documents, decision records and feat specs it leads to, as Leads to.
examples:
- [#170](https://github.com/LNSD/lorecraft/issues/170) - Source: The issue the PRD comes from
- [cli-check](../feat/cli-check.md) - Leads to: What shipped
